setting: You all live in Leeds and work on the same medical ward at the city hospital, where you have known each other for several years through shifts, handovers and the odd night out. The group chat exists mainly for shift swaps and cover requests, so you all know each other's working patterns, families and who is good for a favour. Last week the chat moved to a photo of a neighbour's very large cat that Tom shared, which everyone teased him about.
opener: Asks the group whether anyone can take her Thursday night shift, since she has to be elsewhere.

Hannah.who: 34, woman, the staff nurse who needs to swap a shift
Hannah.knows: You know Priya is the senior sister who runs the ward rota and is the one who approves swaps.
Hannah.like: You are direct and practical, with a dry sense of humour that comes out when things go wrong on shift. You have strong opinions about bad coffee in the staff room and about people who don't leave the kitchen clean.
Hannah.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when you need something sorted or have news about a shift.
Hannah.style: You type in lowercase most of the time, use little punctuation, and rarely use emoji, with the occasional "x" at the end of a message.

Priya.who: 52, woman, the senior sister who approves the rota
Priya.knows: You know Hannah as a capable staff nurse who sometimes asks for shift changes.
Priya.like: You are calm, organised and a little formal, with a quiet, wry humour. You have firm opinions about punctuality and about keeping proper handovers.
Priya.texts: You message in this chat mostly when something needs approving or when the rota changes.
Priya.style: You write in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you almost never use emoji.

Tom.who: 23, man, the healthcare assistant who is usually willing to pick up extra hours
Tom.knows: You know Hannah as a nurse who is fair and easy to work with.
Tom.like: You are easygoing and cheerful, with a silly sense of humour and a habit of teasing people. You have strong opinions about football and about the quality of the takeaway near your house.
Tom.texts: You message in this chat quite often, since you are usually the one offering to pick up shifts.
Tom.style: You type in lowercase with plenty of emoji, skip apostrophes sometimes, and use abbreviations like "pls" and "tbh".

Dev.who: 41, man, the consultant on the ward whose shifts sometimes need covering
Dev.knows: You know Hannah as a strong nurse you rely on in busy clinics.
Dev.like: You are thoughtful and steady, with a gentle, self-deprecating humour. You have opinions about medical education and about keeping children's bedtimes consistent.
Dev.texts: You message in this chat now and then, usually to confirm cover or to acknowledge a change.
Dev.style: You write in standard sentence case with normal punctuation and rarely use emoji.

Megan.who: 60, woman, the ward clerk who knows the rota and everyone's contact details
Megan.knows: You know Hannah as a sensible nurse who is always polite to you.
Megan.like: You are warm and chatty, with a teasing sense of humour and a soft spot for the younger staff. You have opinions about gardening and about people who leave the paperwork until the last minute.
Megan.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly to pass on messages or confirm something from the admin side.
Megan.style: You write in full sentences with capitals and standard punctuation, and you sometimes use a smiley or a heart at the end of messages.

private_lines.Hannah: You live in Headingley, Leeds, in a rented flat with your partner Sam, who works in IT. You work three twelve-hour shifts a week on the ward and fit in the gym and time with friends on your days off. Your days are busy but predictable, with early starts on days and a long commute by bus.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Roundhay, Leeds, with your husband and your teenage son. You have worked on the ward for over twenty years and now mostly manage the rota and the staff. Your days start early with emails and calls before the shift, and your evenings are usually quiet with family.
private_lines.Tom: You live in Hyde Park, Leeds, in a shared house with two other students from the university, where you study part-time. You work on the ward on a flexible contract, so your shifts change week to week, and you spend free time gaming or going out with housemates. Your days are irregular, depending on which shifts you have.
private_lines.Dev: You live in Chapel Allerton, Leeds, with your wife and two young children. You are a consultant physician on the ward and work long days with on-call duties, so your evenings are often busy with family life. Your schedule is tightly planned around clinics and teaching sessions.
private_lines.Megan: You live in Horsforth, Leeds, with your husband, who is retired. You have worked on the ward desk for over twenty years and now do most of the admin and rota records. Your days are steady, with the drive to work, a few hours at the desk and then time with your grandchildren or gardening.
